said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.

It was wonderful to join the Texas Restaurant Association for a roundtable at Eno’s Pizza Tavern in Coppell. We talked about my legislation, the Beverage Regulatory Parity Act, which would establish a federal regulatory framework for hemp-derived beverages.
 
We also discussed how provisions from the Working Families Tax Cuts, like no tax on tips, ensures more money stays in the pockets of their employees.

Recently, I heard from Texas Restaurant Association members at a roundtable in Coppell about the challenges they face as restaurateurs, from supporting their employees to the rules around the products they serve.

Through the Working Families Tax Cuts and no tax on tips, we’re ensuring their employees keep more of what they earn, and I’m working to give North Texas businesses clear guidance with my Beverage Regulatory Parity Act.

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
